title: Indiana ex parte renewal share, August 2026
question: What percentage of Indiana Medicaid and CHIP beneficiaries due for renewal in August 2026 will CMS report as renewed on an ex parte basis in the first published original (O) submission row of dataset 5abea2e0-3f8e-4b49-a50d-d63d5fd9103c, rounded to one decimal?
resolutionSource: CMS, State Medicaid and CHIP Eligibility Processing Data (data.medicaid.gov)
resolutionRule: Resolves to Indiana's ex parte renewal share for the August 2026 reporting period, computed from the original (O) submission row in CMS dataset 5abea2e0-3f8e-4b49-a50d-d63d5fd9103c when CMS first publishes it. Compute 100 times beneficiaries_whose_coverage_was_renewed_on_an_ex_parte_basis divided by beneficiaries_with_a_renewal_due, using the numerator and denominator as first published, and round to one decimal. Later corrections and updated (U) submissions do not change resolution.
drivers: Lower ex parte renewal level since March
Partial recovery in May and June
Two-month forecast horizon from the latest available O row

reasoning.text: Indiana August 2026 ex parte renewal forecast

The target is an Indiana state row for the August 2026 reporting period, using original (O) monthly submissions and first publication. The ledger does not explicitly identify the denominator. I interpret it using CMS's published state ex parte rate: beneficiaries renewed ex parte divided by all beneficiaries due for renewal. All historical anchors use O rows; no updated (U) outcomes enter the forecast.

reasoning.text: The outside-view reference class is the six fetched Indiana O rows for January-June 2026. Their computed ex parte shares are 18.2562%, 17.6841%, 10.7728%, 5.2125%, 7.1955%, and 7.7008%. The six-month base rate is 11.1370%; the April-June average is 6.7030%. The latest level and recent average support a forecast below the full-sample mean.

Separate effects: level follows June's 7.7008%; momentum allows a damped continuation of the May-June recovery; no separate one-off adjustment is imposed. No fetched official evidence establishes a policy or system change that explains the decline, so the policy-mechanism adjustment is zero. Changes in cohort composition or electronic verification remain scenario risks.

Using unrounded shares, the five successive changes are -0.5721, -6.9113, -5.5602, +1.9829, and +0.5053 percentage points. Their sample standard deviation is sqrt(sum((change - mean change)^2)/4) = 3.9024 percentage points. Recent monthly momentum is (1.9829 + 0.5053)/2 = 1.2441. Point = 7.7008 + 0.5 × 2 × 1.2441 = 8.9450. Half-width = 1.28 × 3.9024 × sqrt(2) = 7.0640. Unrounded bounds are 1.8809 and 16.0090; one-decimal outputs are 8.9, 1.9, and 16.0.

Prior/update/interval: The model is June-level persistence with 50% damped recent momentum, using six January-June 2026 original-submission shares. Level prior = 7.7008%; momentum adjustment = +1.2441 percentage points over two months; one-off and policy adjustments = 0. From the five successive historical changes, sigma = 3.9024 percentage points. The normal-approximation 80% half-width starts at 1.28*sigma = 4.9950 and scales by sqrt(2) for the June-to-August horizon, giving 7.0640. Final point is 8.9%, with implied rounded bounds of 1.9%-16.0%.

Upside risk: restored electronic matching or a cohort easier to verify could accelerate the recovery; a return to February's 17.7% would land above the interval. Downside risk: further verification failures or delayed processing could suppress automatic renewals; a near-zero ex parte share would land outside the interval below 1.9%.
